topics.label: My Five Senses
facts: Your five senses are sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
Your eyes help you see colours, shapes, and movement.
Your ears help you hear sounds like music and voices.
Your tongue helps you taste sweet, sour, salty, and bitter foods.

questions.q: How many senses do you have?
questions.fact: Your five senses are sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.

questions.q: Which sense do you use to hear music?
questions.fact: Your ears help you hear sounds.

questions.q: Which part of your body helps you taste food?
questions.fact: Your tongue has tiny taste buds that tell you how food tastes.

questions.q: Which sense do you use to smell a flower?
questions.fact: Your nose helps you smell flowers, food, and many other things.

topics.label: Teeth
facts: Teeth help you bite and chew your food.
Children have 20 baby teeth, and grown-ups have 32 teeth.
Brushing your teeth twice a day keeps them clean and strong.
Too many sweets can give your teeth holes called cavities.

questions.q: What do teeth help you do?
questions.fact: Teeth bite and chew food so you can swallow it safely.

questions.q: How many times a day should you brush your teeth?
questions.fact: Brushing twice a day, morning and night, keeps teeth healthy.

questions.q: What can too many sweets do to your teeth?
questions.fact: Sugar feeds tiny germs that can make holes in teeth.

questions.q: How many baby teeth do children have?
questions.fact: Children have 20 baby teeth, which later fall out to make room for adult teeth.

topics.label: Trees
facts: Trees are big plants with a trunk, branches, and leaves.
Trees make the oxygen we breathe.
Some trees grow fruit, like apples and oranges.
Trees give shade and homes to birds and other animals.

questions.q: What is the thick middle part of a tree called?
questions.fact: The trunk holds the tree up and carries water to the branches.

questions.q: What do trees make that we breathe?
questions.fact: Trees take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen into the air.

questions.q: Which of these grows on a tree?

questions.fact: Many birds build their nests in trees.

topics.label: Healthy Habits
facts: Washing your hands with soap helps wash away germs that can make you sick.
Children need lots of sleep to grow and learn, usually around 9 to 11 hours each night.
Moving your body every day, by playing, running, or dancing, keeps your muscles and heart strong.
Brushing your teeth twice a day helps keep them clean and strong.

questions.q: Why should you wash your hands with soap?
choices: To make them smell nice only
questions.fact: Soap and water wash away germs that can make you sick.

questions.q: How much sleep do children usually need each night?
questions.fact: Most children need about 9 to 11 hours of sleep each night.

questions.q: What does playing and running every day do for your body?
choices: It keeps your muscles and heart strong
questions.fact: Daily play and exercise keep muscles, bones, and your heart strong.

questions.q: How often should you brush your teeth?
questions.fact: Brushing twice a day keeps teeth clean and helps stop tooth decay.
